chunks: And from him, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Ya'qub ibn Shu'ayb, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the *luqatah* (found property), and we were at Mina at that time. He said: 'As for this land of ours, it is not permissible (to keep it without announcing). As for you, the owner is the one who finds it; he announces it for a year in every gathering, and then it is like his wealth.'

key_terms.كَسَبِيلِ مَالِهِ: Like his own wealth / becomes his property
key_terms.يُعَرِّفُهَا: He announces it / makes it known

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling for found property (luqatah) in Mecca versus other places?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) distinguishes the ruling for *luqatah* (found property) between Mecca/Mina and other places. In Mecca, it is not permissible to keep it, whereas elsewhere, the finder announces it for a year in gatherings; if unclaimed, it becomes his property. This ruling reflects the unique sanctity of the Haram, where found items are treated as *bayt al-mal* (public treasury) rather than private property, a distinction rooted in the Prophetic tradition that 'there is no *luqatah* in Mecca.'
